column3: According to Stripe's engineering blog, moving millions of objects from one database table to another is difficult but something many companies need to do. It describes a common four-step dual writing pattern for large online migrations: dual write to the existing and new tables to keep them in sync, change all read paths to read from the new table, change all write paths to write only to the new table, and remove the old data that relies on the outdated data model.

According to the same post, new writes update both stores, and existing objects are copied lazily whenever they are updated before the remaining ones are backfilled. Stripe suggests slowly ramping up the percentage of objects that get duplicated while watching operational metrics, because of the performance impact of the extra write on the production database. For the backfill it finds the objects to migrate with an offline MapReduce job over database snapshots, which has no impact on production, and it runs that job again after the migration to check that no objects are missing.
